stories.title: Somalis Displaced by 2023 Floods Face New Threat as El Niño Looms, WFP Says
stories.description: MOGADISHU, The World Food Programme has warned that communities devastated by the 2023 floods are once again bracing for El Niño and the threat of further flooding, as Somalia enters the Deyr rainy season under a high-risk climate scenario. In a statement posted on social media, WFP shared the testimony of a community member named Ali, whose account of the 2023 disaster and the growing risks facing his community underscores the cyclical nature of Somalia’s climate emergencies. The agency said climate signals currently mirror those that preceded the severe floods of 1997 and 2023, with the Juba and Shabelle river basins facing the highest risk of inundation. The warning comes just days after WFP cautioned that drought conditions from the previous season have left communities with depleted coping mechanisms, making them even more vulnerable to the anticipated rains. The Deyr season, which typically runs from October to December, is expected to bring above-normal rainfall to central and southern Somalia. A Disaster Repeating Itself The 2023 floods were among the most severe in Somalia’s recent history, displacing over a million people and submerging vast areas of farmland in the Juba and Shabelle basins. The disaster followed a prolonged drought that had already pushed millions to the brink of famine, compounding a humanitarian crisis that had barely begun to stabilize. According to the Food and Agriculture Organization, sea surface temperatures in the eastern and central Pacific Ocean are rising, and if warming continues, rainfall could increase significantly, triggering riverine and flash floods in the main river basins. The FAO has warned that historical patterns suggest a high likelihood of an El Niño event, with the Juba and Shabelle rivers carrying the highest risk of severe flooding. stories.title: What's driving Hong Kong's growing Pokemon card craze?
stories.description: Pokemon card collecting is gaining momentum in Hong Kong, with enthusiasts drawn to rare finds. But an economist warns that rising prices for some cards could signal a bubble.

stories.title: 4 USB-C Accessories That Can Eliminate Cable Clutter
stories.description: If you have a lot of cable clutter on your desk, using retractable cables, USB-C hubs, wireless chargers, and power strips with clamps are useful solutions.
